decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom serves a niche but strategic proton/ion market, yet its visibility fell from its own page to a mere mention in 2019, which suggests results below aspiration and justifies elevated but not decisive drop risk.
Small volume ionization chambers are core dosimetry products with steady clinical demand, and the product kept its own page into 2019, so results appear satisfactory and give no trigger for search.
This small field chamber supports growing stereotactic and IMRT workflows within the firm's established dosimetry business and was consistently presented, so management has little reason to drop it.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple reference product with stable aspiration-meeting demand and calibration synergies, so keeping it is the satisficing choice.
Relative dosimetry chambers complement the firm's water phantom and QA platform offerings and showed continued presence, so they appear to meet aspirations.
Thimble chambers are long-lived workhorse products in a firm with ample slack from decades of dosimetry leadership, so dropping one is unlikely absent clear evidence of shortfall.
